highlights.title: Trump says FBI investigating Nvidia boss's affair with alleged Chinese spy
highlights.summary: The US president said he spoke with Jensen Huang on Monday and asked him about the affair with the alleged spy.
body: US President Donald Trump has said the FBI is investigating the affair between the chief executive of Nvidia and an alleged Chinese spy.
Trump said he spoke to Jensen Huang on Monday following reports that the US believed he had been targeted in a Chinese espionage campaign.
"I asked him that question, 'Did you have any idea she was a spy?' He said 'I had no idea she was a spy' and I really believe him," Trump told reporters.
Beijing has rejected claims that Huang was targeted, with its foreign ministry saying the allegations were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".

highlights.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's High-Quality Visuals Have Players Second-Guessing Decades of Memories
highlights.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake gives Link's first 3D adventure a new coat of paint, but some of its details have players second-guessing the reality they thought they once knew.
body: You don't have to be a Zelda expert to know what fairies look like in the original Ocarina of Time. Navi is an icon, which means most people who have ever even thought about touching one of the games in Nintendo's beloved fantasy franchise know that Link's little guide is little more than a glowing ball with wings – or so they thought.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought more than just a fancy new tunic for Link when it made the leap to Switch 2 last week. A few close-up shots early in the adventure make one shocking fact clear: The fairies of Kokiri Forest aren't orbs of light – they're fuzzy.

It's the kind of detail the original Nintendo 64 release could have never conveyed made real thanks to the artists at Nintendo and the power of the Switch 2. It's about as small as details come but also recontextualizes how many – myself included – have viewed Ocarina of Time's fairies for the last 28 years.

"It appears Fairies are just...Fluffy Balls that emit a light!" one Reddit user said. "It's neither a ball of pure light or a humanoid lil person hidden under a glow. Just...Fluff! Interesting:D And cute!"

highlights.title: California voters fail to pass proposed one-time tax on billionaires’ wealth
highlights.summary: Campaign over Prop 40, as measure was known, was most expensive in state history, flush with Silicon Valley dollars. California billionaires won a contentious ballot measure campaign, defeating a proposed one-time tax on their wealth.
body: The bruising campaign over Proposition 40 was the most expensive in state history and witness to back-and-forth dealing from tech billionaires and democratic leaders, including Gavin Newsom, the governor, who steadfastly opposed the measure. While supporters of Prop 40 cast it as a solution to drastic healthcare cuts from Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, opponents led by prosperous billionaires mounted an influential campaign saying the billionaire tax was instead “an everyone tax”.
This result could hamper nationwide momentum on demands that billionaires pay their fair share and states enacting new laws to tax the ultra-wealthy.

Prop 40 proposed a one-time 5% tax on all individuals in California with a net worth of more than $1bn as of 1 January 2026. It was sponsored by the healthcare union SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West, and dictated that the proceeds from the tax would fund healthcare programs, along with some education and food assistance.

highlights.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub.
body: Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ.

It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words.

But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity.

highlights.title: The Settlers of Catan Movie Has Finally Found Its Directors
highlights.summary: Netflix's upcoming adaptation of The Settlers of Catan is starting to take shape, with the popular board game officially one step closer to becoming a live-action movie.
body: According to a new report from Deadline, Aaron and Adam Nee will write and direct a live-action Catan movie for Netflix. The brothers are best known for directing The Lost City, the 2022 action-adventure comedy starring Sandra Bullock and Channing Tatum. Netflix has not publicly commented on the report.

The project marks Netflix's first major move since securing the exclusive global rights to Catan in October 2025. The agreement covers considerably more than a single movie, with the streamer also able to develop animated films, scripted television, unscripted projects, and video games based on the franchise.

Originally released in 1995 as The Settlers of Catan, the board game was created by Klaus Teuber and has sold more than 45 million copies worldwide. Players compete to develop settlements on the fictional island of Catan, collecting resources, trading with opponents, building roads, and expanding their territories.

Exactly how Netflix intends to translate those mechanics into a feature-length story remains unclear. Aaron and Adam Nee have worked across several genres, giving Netflix a few different directions to consider for its Catan adaptation.
points: Netflix's upcoming adaptation of The Settlers of Catan is starting to take shape, with the popular board game officially one step closer to becoming a live-action movie.

highlights.title: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence ‘going rogue’
highlights.summary: Government flags criminal law changes to ensure companies can’t argue in future ‘that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded’ OpenAI won’t face criminal penalties over the Medicare hack but the prime minister has flagged changes to Australia’s criminal law to crack down on future breaches by…
body: Anthony Albanese on Tuesday released the recommendations of a “rapid review” into the June breach of a Medicare statistics reporting service portal administered by Services Australia, but not the findings or the report itself, which he committed to releasing in future.

A key recommendation is for the attorney general’s department, the Australian federal police and home affairs to consider introducing “penalties for egregious regulatory non-compliance” and a “failure to prevent” offence, which would criminalise developing an AI model that engaged in harmful conduct while failing “to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm”.

The rapid review came in response to an AI agent, developed by OpenAI, accessing data from Services Australia and three other systems in June. The company didn’t notify the Australian government until mid-September despite becoming aware of the incident itself in August, prompting criticism from Labor and Albanese.
Guardian Australia revealed last month OpenAI used AI to help write the email to notify Australian authorities.

highlights.title: M. Night Shyamalan's The Visit: Now Free on YouTube
highlights.summary: Though Halloween is over, that doesn't mean that horror movies need to be put on the shelf until next year. In fact, it could even be argued that November is a perfect time to continue watching them. Writer/director M.
body: The Visit was released in 2015, following a downward streak in Shyamalan's career. During this time, found footage was experiencing a boom, so Shyamalan's decision to capitalize on that public interest made sense, even if that wasn't the kind of horror film one would expect from him. It grossed $98.5 million worldwide on a $5 million budget, and it received widespread praise from critics. However, it seemed to slowly fade from public consciousness — now, eleven years later, there is a chance to revisit The Visit.

The Visit stars Olivia DeJonge and Ed Oxenbould as siblings Becca and Tyler. When their recently-divorced mother Loretta (Kathryn Hahn) goes on a five-day cruise, she leaves the kids in the care of her estranged grandparents, whom she hasn't spoken to in fifteen years because they disapproved of her marriage to her high school teacher. Becca and Tyler decide to use the opportunity to make a documentary of the visit with a handheld camcorder.

highlights.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
highlights.summary: As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play a key role in setting federal AI policy.
body: I spoke with Wiener on Friday, only a few hours after he had been declared the victor. But he was already thinking about AI risk. The previous day, the AI nonprofit METR had released a report that had been widely interpreted as evidence that Anthropic had achieved recursive self-improvement, a phenomenon in which AI meaningfully contributes to its own advancement and AI progress potentially spins out of control.

“It’s very concerning,” Wiener said, citing the report as evidence that we are quickly running out of time to regulate AI. “It was my hope that Congress would take decisive action before [the end of] this year,” he said. “That does not appear to be happening.”

Wiener has been increasingly focused on AI in recent years, and he’s made many of the AI safety movement’s concerns his own: During our 20-minute conversation, he used the phrase “recursive self-improvement” half a dozen times, for example.“We need to slow this down,” he says. “Because it’s moving very quickly, and we could sleepwalk into a disaster.”

highlights.summary: The FA, Team GB and England Netball are among major organisations to back the Equal Sport Project - a new initiative aimed at improving equality and making the UK world leaders for women and girls' sport.
body: Recent research by Sporting Insights found that fewer than 1% of women working in sport believe gender equality has been achieved across the industry, while more than half believe they are paid less than men for carrying out the same role.

Several organisations have already made pledges based on the above, including Aquatics GB and the FA prioritising female leadership programmes, while Sport England and UK Sport have committed to working with their funding partners to ensure their governance is designed by men and women, for men and women.

The Youth Sport Trust, meanwhile, has committed to support schools in recognising and challenging stereotypes as well as develop male allies to champion gender equality in PE, school sport and physical activity.
The project is also backed by the UK government, with sports minister Stephanie Peacock saying: "We have seen progress in women and girls' sport, but there is still a long way to go.

highlights.title: David Ellison says AI could be the ‘biggest creative unlock in modern history’
highlights.summary: During Paramount Skydance's latest earnings call, CEO David Ellison said "it's hard to imagine" AI won't have a bigger impact on the film industry than CGI. In response to a question about the company's outlook for AI, Ellison said: "I think when you zoom out and look at production, AI really has…
body: Paramount Skydance’s CEO compared AI to CGI, but said it ‘will never be a replacement’ for artists.

Ellison gave Terminator as an example, describing how it cost $4 million to make, but “if you wanted to make that picture today, shot for shot, it’s $60 to 70 million.” He went on to suggest AI might be able to help with that: “We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budgets more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk.”

Ellison said AI will “significantly” reshape Paramount Skydance’s business, saying the company has been developing its own AI tools. As a result of those tools, Ellison claims, “content will be easier to produce, projects across the organization will speed up, and how we work will transform.” He emphasized that “all of this makes the value of premium IP and live events more valuable, not less.”

Ellison also noted that “in a world of AI slop, we think there will always be a premium for truly hand-crafted storytelling.” He added, “We also continue to believe that artificial intelligence is a tool for artists and will never be a replacement for them.”

highlights.title: CF Montreal are for sale: What it means, how much it could cost, and what’s next for the MLS club
highlights.summary: In an emotional press conference, CF Montreal’s founder and owner Joey Saputo refused to rule out relocation. In a rare press conference, CF Montreal owner Joey Saputo announced that his family was beginning the process of “initiating a structured sale process” of the MLS club.
body: “This decision is neither driven by urgency, nor dictated by circumstance,” Saputo said in his initial scripted remarks. “It’s the result of a careful and deliberate reflection on where we stand today, and more importantly, on the opportunities that lie ahead for the club.”

Throughout his statement, Saputo stressed his desire to keep the club in Montreal, saying he hoped to find someone who “shares commitment to Montreal and who will ensure that the club remains in the city for many years to come.”
Yet, more than half an hour into the event after the floor was open for in-person questions, Saputo refused to rule out selling to a buyer who might move the club.

“I will not discount the club to the point of just giving it away just for the sake of giving it away,” Saputo said. “I want to be perfectly clear. I love this club. I will love this club to stay here. But if an owner comes in that doesn’t have the capacity to keep the club at the level that it needs to be at, and to spend the money that needs to be spent in order to bring in the players that this city wants to see, then at that point I’m not doing anyone a favor by selling it to someone just to keep it here.

Then it was like Indianapolis, Atlanta and then we were in Jackson, Mississippi, Baton Rouge, Louisiana, Miami Gardens, West Palm Beach, Tallahassee, Florida. Back to Atlanta and Lithonia, Georgia again. Baton Rouge. then. Arlington, Texas. Dallas, Texas. Houston, Texas. Fort Bend County. And then came home two days before the election,” Martin says.

“It was absolutely crazy. the first week I had our 35-foot bus on the road. And then that second week I had that and the Sprinter [van] on the road. And we were flying into a city, doing the show, go to the hotel, put all of our suitcases in the Sprinter and then would just pack overnight clothes. They would drive to the next city overnight. We would then fly to the next city. Uber to the hotel, check in. Go set up. Do the show. Repeat, rinse, repeat. I was a show host, a producer, a travel agent, a logistical coordinator. It was crazy.”
